sources_and_data.source: Reidl-Wahlstrom, Parameterized Algorithms for Zero Extension and Metric Labelling Problems
sources_and_data.use: source exact k-bounded metric-labeling objective and contraction-based upper-bound context
audited distinction between source construction and arbitrary sparsifier models
restricted cactus theorem independently counted again here

method.type: direct mathematical proof and adversarial review; no experiment
method.contraction_model: quotient by an edge set whose connected bags contain at most one terminal; loops deleted, parallel edges retained, no new vertices or edges
method.objective_quantifiers: all finite metrics with |D|<=s, all injective terminal labelings, fixed integer k, exact restricted optimum including +infinity
method.family: B_(r,t): t internally vertex-disjoint length-two paths for every terminal pair
method.parameters: r>=2, t>=1, L=t*binomial(r,2), terminal count r<=s

mathematical_claim: For B_(r,t), every terminal-preserving contraction quotient has at least L=t*binomial(r,2) non-loop edges, and every such quotient preserves the exact objective. The family therefore proves a feasible Omega(k) contraction-only lower bound when L<=k, but cannot produce a k^(Omega(s)) exponent because feasibility itself forces L<=k.
assumptions: Graphs are finite undirected multigraphs and parallel-edge multiplicity is counted separately.
A contraction quotient may not merge two terminals and may not add or delete non-loop edges.
Terminal labels are injective, so every terminal pair in B_(r,t) receives distinct metric points.
The source-level arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifier model is not identified with this quotient model.
The cactus counting audit uses a finite connected standard cactus and the already proved local preservation lemmas.
verified_steps: The exact restricted optimum of B_(r,t) is t times the sum of terminal-pair distances when k>=L and is +infinity when k<L.
Triangle inequality gives one-crossing and endpoint-distance lower bounds for every length-two path.
Terminal preservation forbids contracting both edges of any terminal-pair path, so every path contributes at least one quotient edge.
Joint contractions cannot merge distinct paths because their internal vertices have no cross-path edges.
Every allowed quotient has the same exact objective as the original pair-bundle graph.
The feasible choice r=2,t=k gives a fully proved Omega(k) lower bound independent of the label-budget exponent.
The infeasible choice L>k gives an unbounded-size obstruction for a total pure quotient model, exposing a representation mismatch rather than an s-dependent lower bound.
The cactus counting argument was independently charged to terminal markers and block-cut incidences, yielding O(|S|) retained edges.
gaps: No feasible contraction-only family with a lower bound growing as k^(Omega(s)) was constructed or ruled out.
No transfer theorem to arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers was attempted or established.
The source's exact handling of infeasible instances must be modeled separately before comparing total quotient bounds.

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Pairwise distinct edge signatures alone force one retained edge per signature and an s-dependent exponent.
counterexamples.counterexample: B_(r,t) has distinguishable terminal-pair path signatures, but one contraction per path yields exactly L parallel terminal edges and preserves every metric and labeling.
counterexamples.scope: Refutes the inference, not the existence of all possible s-dependent families.

uncertainty: The Omega(k) result is for the explicit contraction-only quotient model, not the unrestricted sparsifier model.
The infeasible-instance unboundedness is a model obstruction and may disappear under a source-style no-instance replacement convention.
The broad feasible-instance s-dependence question remains open.

proof_status.scope: The pair-bundle lower-bound proposal and pairwise-signature inference are resolved; the general O7 conjecture remains open.
excluded_claims: No k^(Omega(s)) lower bound is claimed.
No lower bound for arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers is claimed.
No computational or asymptotic evidence beyond the displayed proof is claimed.

independent_review.review_type: adversarial review of quotient definition, all contraction patterns, metrics, crossing feasibility, multiplicity, joint contractions, and cactus counting
reviewed_failure_modes: contracting both edges of a path and merging terminals
cross-path or joint contractions creating an uncounted shortcut
metric choices violating positivity or triangle inequality
hidden terminal- or label-budget dependence in the cactus count
independent_review.review_conclusion: The restricted pair-bundle theorem and the obstruction to the pairwise-signature inference are sound within scope; the broad feasible s-dependent lower-bound problem remains explicitly open.

observed_result_or_blocker.result: A rigorous Omega(k) contraction-only lower bound and an unbounded infeasible-instance quotient obstruction were proved; no s-dependent exponent survives this construction.
observed_result_or_blocker.negative_finding: The proposed pairwise-signature route does not establish a superconstant exponent in s.
observed_result_or_blocker.next_mathematical_question: Find or rule out a feasible joint-contraction hitting-set family with omega(k) quotient size for fixed s>=3, then quantify its s dependence.
observed_result_or_blocker.cactus_count_audit: Independently verified O(|S|) retained block-cut nodes, O(|S|) cycle boundary arcs, and O(|S|) compressed-corridor edges.

paper3_state_check: Paper 3 Target A and Target B unchanged; no historical label or forecast score edited.
next_falsifiable_action: Attempt THEORY-ZEROEXT-FEASIBLE-CONTRACTION-LOWER-BOUND-002: prove or refute an omega(k) feasible joint-contraction lower bound for fixed s>=3, with explicit metrics and no infeasible-instance shortcut.
